name: Peru
sources: GDP $26.4bn and 22.0m people (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, 1990; exact prints $26.410bn and 22,014,771). The dollar figure is the least reliable in this file: with the inti collapsing and a split exchange market, any dollar conversion of Peruvian output in 1990 is an artefact of which rate is used, and estimates run from roughly $22bn to $30bn. Real GDP fell 5.1% in 1990 on top of 12.3% in 1989, a cumulative contraction of about a quarter over three years, hence a TFP trend of -1.5%/yr.

INFLATION IS NOT THE TRANSCRIBED PRINT. INEI records 7,650% for 1990 as an annual average, the worst in Peruvian history and the second worst in the hemisphere after Nicaragua. On the fraction-of-1 convention that is 76.5, twenty-five times the 3.0 ceiling economy.rs clamps to on the first tick. The file ships 2.950 and records the truth here, exactly as brazil.json, poland.json and yugoslavia.json do.

interest_rate 2.9 is a stand-in on the same grounds: nominal rates tracked inflation into the thousands of percent, and the schema's coupling rule forbids entering them beside a clamped inflation figure. The Fujishock of 8 August 1990 that ended this is not scripted; the sim's central bank has to find the stabilisation itself.
Tax take 9% of GDP: central government tax revenue had fallen to about 8.1% of GDP by 1989-90, near the point at which a state stops functioning, which is the substantive fact this row carries.

Debt 0.80: external debt about $20bn at end-1990 (World Bank), roughly 76% of GDP and in arrears since Alan Garcia capped debt service at 10% of export earnings in July 1985 and the IMF declared Peru ineligible in 1986.
Oil 0.13 mbd: about 130,000 bbl/d from the northern jungle and Talara, down by a third from the early 1980s.

Stability 22, the lowest figure in this roster, and it is transcribed: Sendero Luminoso and the MRTA held emergency-zone provinces containing over half the population, the war had killed some 20,000 people by 1990, and cholera arrived in January 1991. Separatism 0.06 — Sendero sought to replace the state, not to leave it. Defence 2.3% of GDP, strength 6, an army fighting an internal war it was not built for.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.3466%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series PER (Peru): 19,174,716 in 1984 to 21,532,589 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 1.597 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, PER, 1989: US$1597167000.00 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: PER.
AUTHORED, AND THE ANSWER IS NOTHING. Both named series were checked and both refused this nation; the empty grant list is a finding, not an absence of work.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 72% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: refused.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 0 against a threshold of any positive count: refused.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.
